answers:
Accessing virtual private endpoints (VPEs) from an on-premises network or another VPC can be achieved through IBM Cloud Direct Link or IBM Cloud Transit Gateway. VPEs are created in a separate, dedicated subnet within your VPC and can be accessed remotely using the IP addresses of your choice. To access a VPE from another subnet, you need to configure your network ACLs or security groups to allow cross-subnet access. Only TCP services are supported for VPEs.
When accessing VPE from a remote client through Direct Link, you must configure DNS forwarding rules for the private endpoints that you want to access through VPE, to the custom resolver provisioned in the VPC where VPE gateways are created. When accessing VPE from a remote client through Transit Gateway, you must also provision a custom resolver in the VPC where the client is running, and configure DNS forwarding rules to the custom resolver provisioned in the VPC where VPE gateways are created.

IBM Cloud and Cloudflare provide Cloud Internet Services (CIS) that ensure workload isolation by maintaining separate zones and domains for different customers within individual subaccounts in the CIS account at Cloudflare. Access to these accounts and the CIS control plane infrastructure is strictly limited to essential maintenance personnel only. 
Data stored at Cloudflare is encrypted, except in cases where public access is necessary, such as with DNS records. How can I create an endpoint gateway?

You can create an endpoint gateway for an IBM Cloud® service that you wish to access on your private VPC network using the user interface (UI), command-line interface (CLI), or application programming interface (API).
Before you begin, it's important to review the section on planning for virtual private endpoint gateways. After the endpoint gateway is created, you can modify the security groups associated with it, such as applying specific security group rules to the data paths of the endpoint gateway.
What do you do to configure ACLs for use with Endpoint Gateways?

To configure Access Control Lists (ACLs) for use with Endpoint Gateways, it is best to do this before performing any actions on a virtual private endpoint (VPE), such as creating or updating it. The ACL is applied to the subnet containing the reserved IP linked to the endpoint gateway, which creates the VPE. Please ensure that the same rule is applied to each subnet with an endpoint connected to the VPE. This can be accomplished by using the same ACL across all the subnets or by establishing a rule in each of the different ACLs for the same VPE if they are located on different subnets.
